User-defined class named `Enum` is incorrectly inferred as `enum.Enum`

Tested in Python 3.10.16

When I define my own class named `Enum` and try to use it, astroid incorrectly infers it as the built-in `enum.Enum` class instead of my custom class.

```python
# Define a custom Enum class
class Enum:
    def __init__(self, one, two):
        self.one = one
        self.two = two
    
    def pear(self):
        pass

# Try to use it
my_enum = Enum("apple", "orange")

# Expected: my_enum should be an instance of my custom Enum class
# Actual: my_enum is inferred as an instance of enum.Enum
```

This causes problems when trying to access attributes or methods that exist in my custom class but not in the built-in enum.Enum class. For example, trying to call `my_enum.pear()` would fail because astroid thinks it's a built-in enum.

The issue seems to be that astroid is prioritizing the built-in enum.Enum over user-defined classes with the same name.

Scope of this editing session: update the following production files and report the resulting local change for handover: astroid/brain/brain_namedtuple_enum.py. No full task validation has been performed in this session.
